page.layout: One page of text. At the top, two round portrait medallions side by side. Below them, one column of running text in two paragraphs. No margin notes, no footnotes.

main_text.p: MARCILIVS Ficinus, Patria Florentinus diuinæ Philosophiæ amore incẽsus, Platonis vniuersum opus, maxima diligẽtia trástulit. Erat corpore admodũ pusillo, víxque semihominem æquare videbatur, sed tamen acuto ingenio erat prędi-tus, & vtriusq; linguæ admirabili facultate. Vnde Plotinũ, Iamblicũ, Synefium, & Psellum Platonicæ sectæ nobiles authores, Latinos effecit, hortante Cofmo Medice, & suffragantibus his qui Cofmo successerunt, à quibus, multis numeribus sese adau-ctũ & cumulatè ornatũ sensit. Fuit lætus & ad tuēda valetudi-nē exactus. Scripsit plures libros, qui feruntur Theologiæ naturalis lib. 1. de intelleƐtu & intelligentia lib.1. in conuiuiũ Platonis lib.1.Epistolarũ lib.plures, de triplici vita lib.tres, Apologiã, in qua agitur de Medicina & Astrologia, quod ad sacerdotes pertineant:&de vita mũdi, deque Magia & Magis, qui Christũ statim natũ salutarunt. Antidotũ Epidemiorũ & præseruatione secũdæ valetudinis, è Græco transtulit in Latinũ, lib. Xenocratis Platonici, de morte, Speusippi Alcinoi, & Pythagoræ opuscula traduxit, & multa alia. Claruit anno 1490. Tandem in Caregiana ipsius villa septuagenario prouectior febricula interiit.

ANGELVS Politianus à iuuentute admirabilis ingenij nomen adeptus est, quũ nouo, illustríque Poëmate Iuliani Medicis equestres ludos celebrasset, Luca Pulcio nobili Poëta omniũ cõfessione superato. Post edita Miscellaneorũ centuriã, publicatáq; Latina Poëmata, immatura mors eũ oppressit, vix qua dragefimũ quartũ ætatis annũ excedētē. Scripsit Epistolarũ lib. 12. miscellaneorũ centuriã 1. Transtulit in Latinã linguã Herodianũ historicũ, Enchiridion Epicteti, cum defensione ad Barthol. Scalam. Alexandri Aphrodisæi, super nonnullis Physicis dubitationibus, solutionum libr. 1. Plutarchi Chæronei amatorias narrationes: & multa alia, quæ excusa reperiuntur Lugduni apud Sebastianum Gryphium. Floruit circiter annum salutis humanæ 1483.

page.notes: Two round engraved medallion portraits at the top, without printed text in the body. Their engraved legends read "MARS. FICINVS" (left) and "ANGELVS POLITIANVS" (right). "excedētē" and the year "1483" (printed with an old-style 3) are doubtful readings. The Greek and Hebrew checks found nothing on this page.
